title: Native return restriction on a specified clopen support
statement: Let k₁/k₀ be a finite extension of finite fields and ℓ an invertible prime. Let X/k₀ be smooth and finite type and C/k₁ geometrically connected and finite type. Let c:C→X be an open and closed immersion commuting with the field-extension maps [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. There exists an exact functor R between the source constructible pro-etale Weil-sheaf categories [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex] on X/k₀ and C/k₁, preserving lissity [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves] and satisfying HasPointwisePowerTransport R c [def-zl-source-constant-field-restriction]. For every arithmetically simple lisse V on X with a nonzero stalk at c(z) for some finite point z of C, R(V) is arithmetically simple lisse. The scheme C and its embedding are supplied; no support or positive-dimensional model is constructed.

proof.text: Put r=[k₁:k₀], so r>0 and #k₁=(#k₀)^r. Construct v from the structural square by exists_clopen_return_geometric_map. Take R to be poweredGeometricPullback v r hv. Its existing instances prove finite-limit and finite-colimit preservation, and its lissity theorem supplies the lisse clause.

proof.text: A zero restricted sheaf has zero stalk at z, by the stalk and coefficient functors. The pointwise Frobenius-module equivalence would make the specified nonzero source stalk subsingleton, a contradiction. To prove simplicity, lift each lisse subobject G→R(V) to U→V by exists_lisse_subobject_clopen_return. Source simplicity says U is zero or its injection is an isomorphism. In the first case exact R preserves its zero object and e gives IsZero G. In the second R maps the source injection to an isomorphism, and canceling e.hom gives IsIso i.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_clopen_return_restriction
    {k₀ k₁ : Type u} [Field k₀] [Finite k₀] [Field k₁] [Finite k₁]
    [Algebra k₀ k₁] {l : ℕ} [Fact l.Prime]
    [Fact (ringChar k₀ ≠ l)] [Fact (ringChar k₁ ≠ l)]
    {X C : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))]
    [C.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k₁))]
    [Smooth (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))]
    [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))]
    [GeometricallyConnected (C ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₁))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (C ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₁))]
    [QuasiCompact (C ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₁))]
    (c : C ⟶ X) [IsOpenImmersion c] [IsClosedImmersion c]
    (hc : c ≫ (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀)) =
      (C ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₁)) ≫
        Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k₀ k₁))) :
    ∃ (R : WeilSheaf k₀ l X ⥤ WeilSheaf k₁ l C)
      (_ : PreservesFiniteLimits R) (_ : PreservesFiniteColimits R),
      (∀ F : WeilSheaf k₀ l X, F.IsLisse → (R.obj F).IsLisse) ∧
      HasPointwisePowerTransport R c ∧
      ∀ (V : WeilSheaf k₀ l X), V.IsIrreducibleLisse →
        ∀ z : C.finitePoints,
          Nontrivial (V.stalk ⟨c z.1, Scheme.Hom.map_mem_finitePoints c z.2⟩).carrier →
          (R.obj V).IsIrreducibleLisse
